text.p: Italian debt markets continued at their low levels of the morning but traders said they had held up slightly better than other markets in the course of the day.
The spread between the benchmark 10-year Btp and the Bund closed in a fraction to 175 from 178 basis points earlier.
"If the other markets keep going down then we'll see the Btp follow," one broker at a U.S. bank in London said.
The March Btp future on LIFFE was 63 basis points off at 127.85 with support plotted just below that level and then loewr at 127.40 and 127.20, traders said.
The July 2006 Btp ended 69 basis points off at 108.40.
Dealers said the impetus for the market had mostly come from abroad but they noted two factors which could have lent a little support to Italian bonds while those about them fell.
Foreign minister and former prime minister Lamberto Dini said the Italian economy was in need of lower interest rates and this was the right moment. Dini is also a former central banker.

Then the government said the OECD, in a report due to be released next week, saw Italy's bid to reduce the deficit/GDP ratio to three percent in 1997 as "credible". Earlier employers' body Confindustria said Italy would fall short of 3.0 percent, warning it would be 4.8 percent without a mini-budget next year.
After markets closed, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said the country's budget deficit would not reach 140 trillion by the year end, as some newspapers have speculated it would.
